paragraphs.text: Masotti et al. (2008) described auriculocondylar syndrome as a disorder of the first and second pharyngeal arches. It is characterized by malformed ears ('question mark ears'), prominent cheeks, microstomia, an abnormal temporomandibular joint, and hypoplasia of the mandibular condyle. Romanelli Tavares et al. (2022) also listed micrognathia as a characteristic feature, and glossoptosis as a less common one. Masotti et al. (2008) noted high phenotypic variation both within and between families.

paragraphs.text: Masotti et al. (2008) found evidence for genetic heterogeneity of auriculocondylar syndrome, suggesting that at least 2 loci are responsible for the phenotype.

checks.claim: There is evidence for genetic heterogeneity of auriculocondylar syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: our results led to the mapping of a first locus of ACS (ACS1) and also showed evidence for genetic heterogeneity

checks.claim: At least 2 loci are suggested to be responsible for the auriculocondylar syndrome phenotype.
checks.evidence_quote: suggesting that there are at least two loci responsible for this phenotype

paragraphs.text: Romanelli Tavares et al. (2022) noted that PLCB4 is the gene most commonly mutated in individuals with auriculocondylar syndrome, followed by GNAI3 and EDN1. All 3 genes belong to the endothelin-1/endothelin receptor type A (EDN1-EDNRA) pathway, which is responsible for patterning the mandibular domain of the first pharyngeal arch.
